firstSection.copytitle: Keeping Websites Accessible,Secure, and Reliable
firstSection.text:
Leveraging my web development experience, I’m currently expanding my expertise in the fundamentals of web security, web accessibility and universal design.
I believe a website's value does not end at launch—it grows through continuous improvement and long-term maintenance. My goal is to help create websites that remain secure, and easy to use for everyone by improving their quality over time.

faq.question: What kind of engineering experience do you have?
faq.answer:
I have worked across both backend development and web development throughout my career.

Before 2016, I worked as a backend engineer, where I specialized in identifying root causes and solving technical problems.
In 2016, I transitioned into web development because I wanted to improve not only the underlying systems but also the design and overall user experience of websites.

faq.question: What were your responsibilities in web development?
faq.answer:
I was responsible for website implementation, WordPress integration, and post-launch maintenance.

Using design files created in Adobe Illustrator, I hand-coded websites from scratch, integrated them into WordPress, and managed deployment.
After launch, I continuously improved website quality through UI/UX enhancements, performance optimization, WordPress maintenance, feature updates, and accessibility improvements.
As the sole technical specialist on the team, I translated requests from non-technical directors into technical requirements, identified root causes, and proposed and implemented effective solutions based on the website's architecture.

faq.question: What do you focus on when designing and implementing websites?
faq.answer:
I focus on building websites with consistency and long-term maintainability in mind.

Beyond creating websites that are intuitive and accessible for everyone, I strive to understand the principles behind both the design and the implementation, ensuring consistency throughout the entire site.
By organizing information, using semantic markup, and building reusable structures, I create websites that are easier to maintain, scale, and evolve over time.

faq.question: What kind of work did you do to improve website quality after launch?
faq.answer:
I continuously worked on improving and maintaining website quality after launch.

Even after a website is launched, ongoing content updates and feature enhancements inevitably introduce new challenges.
In addition to handling content updates and feature enhancements, I was responsible for resolving issues that arise during the operational phase, including WordPress and PHP version upgrades, log analysis for unexpected incidents, and continuous performance optimization after launch.
Rather than simply fixing individual issues, I focused on improvements that considered long-term maintainability and overall quality, helping ensure websites remain reliable and easy for users to continue using over time.

faq.question: What kind of engineer do you aspire to become?
faq.answer:
I aim to become an engineer who continuously improves the quality of websites after launch.

Building on my experience with continuous post-launch improvements throughout my web development career, I want to deepen my expertise and find value in improving the quality, maintainability, and security of websites.
My goal is to help create web services that users can continue to use with confidence over the long term.

VisualThinking.text:
As part of exploring my personal roots, I have published a research article on the "Community of Mixed-Heritage Orphans in 1970s Nagoya and Its Cultural Evolution", a history my grandparents were closely involved in.

Given the sensitive nature of this topic, I approached the research with strict objectivity, prioritizing diverse viewpoints.
I gathered a wide range of sources, from rare books to international research papers, carefully cross-checking them to ensure historical accuracy.

Through this project, I learned to view individual events not as detached points, but as elements connected to a larger surface, mapping them within a broader social and structural context.
This structural thinking directly translate into my web development work today.
In my daily practice, I rely on official Google documentation and technical community insights to ensure reliable system operation, maintenance, and optimization.

At the same time, I love using creative medium as a language to express my inner state and connect deeply.
On my days off, drawing inspiration from zines and museum visits, I have worked on various projects, including image processing, digital art, video editing, and creative coding.
I am particularly drawn to spirituality and the inner world, continuously researching and reinterpreting.
